records.question: What range of coral cover is reported for the reef front off The Rainmaker Hotel at depths between 10 and 25 feet (3 to 8 m)?
ground_truth_chunks: Colonies of a sea anemone (matamalu; <u>Rhodactis</u> sp.), as well as other anemones and anemone fish, are conspicuous on the reef front off The Rainmaker Hotel at depths between 10 and 25 feet (3 to 8 m). Coral cover ranges from 20% to 40%.

records.question: What are the approximate depth and width of the channel that parallels the shoreline north of Anape'ape'a Point?
records.ground_truth_answer: The channel is about 3 feet (1 m) deep and 20 to 30 feet (6 to 9 m) wide.
ground_truth_chunks: A channel about 3 feet (1 m) deep and 20 to 30 feet (6 to 9 m) wide parallels the shoreline.

records.question: What map number is shown in the EASTERN DISTRICT section?
What percentage of the reef front at a depth of 30 feet off the northwestern tip of Fagafue Bay mouth is covered by coral?
ground_truth_chunks: Coral, mostly Acropora, covers 75 to 80% of the reef front at a depth of 30 feet (9 m), off the northwestern tip of Fagafue Bay mouth.

records.question: What are the depth ranges within the channel of Avatele Passage?
records.ground_truth_answer: Depths range from 3 to 26 feet (1 to 8 m).
ground_truth_chunks: The outer portion of Avatele Passage includes a narrow, meandering channel along the southern This channel is approximately 985 feet (300 m) long.
Tidal currents are strong within the channel. Depths range from 3 to 26 feet (1 to 8 m) and the bathymetry is highly irregular.

records.question: Why are the sea cliffs on Ofu generally higher than those on Ta'u?
records.ground_truth_answer: Perhaps because of a longer period of volcanic quiescence or a greater amount of more easily eroded tuff material.

records.question: How wide is the "boat channel" just off the beach north of Pouono Point?
ground_truth_chunks: This rubble and sand-bottom "boat channel" is 10 to 20 feet (3 to 6 m) wide and bordered seaward by a consolidated reef platform.

records.question: What is the major point of access for offshore fishing along the northeast coast of Ta'u Island?
records.ground_truth_answer: Maia Beach is the major point of access for offshore fishing along the northeast coast of Ta'u Island.
ground_truth_chunks: Maia Beach is the major point of access for offshore fishing along the northeast coast. Net fishing occurs off Maia Beach.
Access to the open ocean is through a rip channel. Breakers across this channel limit safe exit and entry to infrequent periods of calm seas (ASCRI).
